meta.normalization: casefold + NFKD ascii-fold + smart-quote/dash-to-ascii fold + strip periods + collapse whitespace; None/'' treated as equal; middle scored as first character of normalised middle (an initial); display_name uses the same normalisation (so period/spacing style does not count as a mismatch).
meta.per_source_grouping: 'by_parser_source' uses the 4 parser_source routing values (house_csv/payroll_comma/senate/display) as literally requested; 'by_source_tag' uses the 6 raw source values (adds lda/quorum/politico/littlesis, all display-routed) and is how the LittleSis slice and the payroll_comma/senate SOURCE_TAG double-count are exposed.

source_tag_mismatch_slice.description: Rows whose sample `source` tag does not match the `parser_source` the parser actually routed them through. All 6 are source=payroll_comma, parser_source=senate (Senate 'LAST, FIRST M' strings tagged as House payroll_comma). Counted in by_parser_source['senate'] AND in by_source_tag['payroll_comma'] above -- this block isolates just them.

Rule 8's display_name() deliberately never renders nickname_raw; gold expects the nickname quoted inline ('Patricia "Trish" Reilly'). Separately, nickname_raw itself also has a leftover-punctuation defect here: the raw's nickname is paren-delimited with an inner literal quote pair ('("TRISH")'), and the paren-capture group keeps the inner quote marks verbatim, so parser nickname_raw is the literal string '"TRISH"' instead of 'TRISH'. The task's normalization spec strips periods but not quote characters, so this scores as an additional nickname_raw mismatch on top of the display_name one.
